subject: Unscheduled maintenance impact — request for downtime confirmation and credit evaluation
messages:
From: Lara Whitman <lara@brewerpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 23:16:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: checkout failures during what looked like unscheduled maintenance

Diego / Marissa,

Heads up — our payments team started seeing a spike of failed checkout requests around 2028-07-19 22:58 - 23:12 UTC (approx). Customers reported 502/503 responses and several timeouts. We reverted a local retry change after noticing the errors — Ive attached a screenshot of the merchant dashboard showing the failure spike.

Can you confirm whether Redwood performed any maintenance or routing change in eu-west-1 during that window? We need an official downtime confirmation and to understand whether this qualifies for an SLA credit.

What we need from Redwood:
- A definitive confirmation of the impacted window (start/end)
- Whether this was an intentional maintenance or an unplanned incident
- Preliminary guidance on SLA credit eligibility and how to request it
- Any immediate mitigations you applied (fallbacks, rollbacks)

Im including our ops contact ops@brewerpay.com if you need raw traces.

Thanks — this is high priority for our incident review tomorrow.

--
Lara Whitman
Head of Payments, BrewerPay
[attachment: checkout_error_20280719.png (image/png)]
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lara Whitman <lara@brewerpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: checkout failures during what looked like unscheduled maintenance

Lara — thanks for the report and the screenshot. Im sorry for the disruption. Ive looped in Rishi (SRE) and Marissa (CS) to pull the telemetry and validate the window.

Quick asks so we can expedite:
- Can you confirm the most representative merchant/customer id and a sample transaction id from the spike?
- If you can share raw request ids/trace ids well correlate with our traces (ops@brewerpay.com is fine).

Were treating this as a potential unscheduled outage until we confirm the cause. Ill follow up with an initial impact window and whether this meets the SLA definition of "unavailable" vs transient errors.

I plan to provide a preliminary impact window within 4 business hours and an RCA timeline by EOD your time.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Account Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Whitman <lara@brewerpay.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:32:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Urgent: checkout failures during what looked like unscheduled maintenance

Lara, Diego,

Preliminary check from our monitoring: there was a short spike of 5xx responses in eu-west-1 between 2028-07-19T22:56:30Z and 2028-07-19T23:11:20Z (approx). Ive attached the monitor export (aggregate by 30s) — it shows a throughput dip and increased error rate starting just before 22:58Z.

What were seeing so far:
- Error class: 502/503 from the serving layer, concentrated on a small subset of hosts handling your shard.
- Likely trigger: a failed rolling network update that caused a brief routing mismatch and KV cache misses; that resulted in a cascade for some long-tail requests.
- Immediate mitigation: autoscaler adjusted and we rerouted traffic away from affected hosts at 23:11Z which brought errors down.

Next steps were taking:
1) Correlate your sample transaction ids to our request traces (Rishi)
2) Pull raw connection-level logs and host timelines for the affected pool
3) Prepare a short incident summary and proposed credit calc if the window meets SLA thresholds

Im attaching: redwood_monitoring_export_20280720.csv (aggregate error/throughput time series).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_monitoring_export_20280720.csv (text/csv)]
From: Lara Whitman <lara@brewerpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brewerpay.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: checkout failures during what looked like unscheduled maintenance

Thanks Marissa — attaching the sample transaction bundle. The spike impacted multiple customers; Ive included three representative transaction ids and a small JSON with request/response payloads. Our compliance team will need the official downtime window and the exact SLA clause youre applying to calculate credits.

Attachments: brewerpay_transaction_sample_07-19.json

Lara
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lara Whitman <lara@brewerpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance impact — request for downtime confirmation and credit evaluation

Lara — thanks for the samples and patience. Short update and request for closure items: 

1) Confirmed preliminary impact window: 2028-07-19T22:56:30Z to 2028-07-19T23:11:20Z (15 minutes). Our investigation classifies this as an unplanned routing/reg-net update that produced transient host-level failures.

2) SLA applicability: based on the window and the error profile, this incident is eligible for an SLA remedy under the "Availability" clause. We will provide a calculated credit amount once the final trace correlation completes (Rishi is finishing the per-request reconciliation).

3) Deliverables and timeline:
   - Today (EOD UTC): formal incident summary (short RCA) and confirmed downtime window (official statement you can share with compliance).
   - +48 hours: full log bundle and per-transaction reconciliation report for the sample ids you provided.
   - Credit calculation: we will include the exact formula and payment timing in the incident summary.

Action for BrewerPay: please confirm whether youd like the formal incident summary sent with a signed statement (for audit) — we can include the credit calculation and payment schedule in the same document. If you need the timeline expedited, we can prioritize the reconciliation.

Im marking this as an incident and will open a formal SLO claim ticket on your behalf. Reference: DP-9812.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Account Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[attachment: incident_prelim_request_form.pdf (application/pdf) — attached by SRE for audit reference]
